assertion.hypothesis_label: HPV-Independent Aldehyde and Replication-Stress Driven Oral Carcinogenesis
assertion.description: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in Fanconi anemia arises predominantly through an HPV-independent route in which endogenous aldehydes (acetaldehyde, formaldehyde) and replication stress in FA-deficient oral keratinocytes generate structural chromosomal variation and copy-number driven, low point-mutation-burden tumors, with premalignant leukoplakia as the visible intermediate. Competing hypotheses are an HPV-driven route and a chronic-inflammation or graft-versus-host-mediated route after transplantation.
assertion.notes: The entry explains HNSCC only through the generic Epithelial Cancer Susceptibility node and separately models HPV-Mediated Epithelial Damage; the relative contribution of the two routes and the aldehyde step are the open mechanistic questions. OpenScientist hypothesis-search report of 2026-09-13: provider and assessor verdicts partially supported. The HPV-independent route and the structural-variant and copy-number driven genomics are supported; the low-SNV inference is qualified because PMID:36450981 attributes it most likely to earlier cancer onset; leukoplakia as premalignant intermediate is supported; the endogenous-aldehyde step in oral keratinocytes is unconfirmed, evidenced only in hematopoietic cells. The provider wrongly recorded the FA-versus-sporadic matched genomic comparison as absent; it is the central result of PMID:36450981. EMERGING retained. Assessment: kb/hypotheses/Fanconi_Anemia/fa_hnscc_hpv_independent_keratinocyte_carcinogenesis/assessments/openscientist-assessment-by-claude-code.yaml.

assertion.name: Pancytopenia
assertion.description: Progressive decline in all blood cell lineages due to bone marrow failure.
assertion.notes: Decreased levels of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Over 80% of FA patients develop bone marrow failure. Typically presents in the first decade, often initially with thrombocytopenia or leukopenia. Notably, patients with FANCD1/BRCA2 mutations may not develop BMF. FA-S (biallelic BRCA1) patients also characteristically lack bone marrow failure.

phenotype_contexts.notes: Over 80% of FA patients develop bone marrow failure.
Neither FANCD1/BRCA2 patient in the Israeli cohort developed BMF. One was transplanted for AML before age 6 months; the other had no complications by age 17.
FA-S (biallelic BRCA1) patients characteristically lack bone marrow failure, distinguishing them from most other FA complementation groups.

The ALDH2*2 dominant-negative variant (rs671), carried by nearly half of the Japanese population, is associated with accelerated BMF progression in FA patients. Birth weight and physical abnormalities were not affected.

assertion.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
assertion.description: Markedly increased risk of early-onset squamous cell carcinomas, particularly of the head and neck, oral cavity, esophagus, and anogenital regions.
assertion.notes: Cancer surveillance is critical due to genomic instability and persistent epithelial cancer risk. Solid tumors in the Israeli cohort appeared at a mean age of 26.6 years, significantly later than MDS/leukemia. All solid tumors in that cohort were in patients with FANCA mutations or undiagnosed patients. HPV vaccination is recommended to reduce risk. Oral examination every 6 months from age 9-10 years and annual nasolaryngoscopy from age 10 years are recommended.

onset.notes: Solid tumors appear significantly later than hematologic malignancies.

phenotype_contexts.notes: All solid tumors in the Israeli cohort were in patients with FANCA mutations or undiagnosed patients. Mean age of solid tumor onset was 26.6 years, significantly later than MDS/leukemia.

Female FA patients have elevated risk of gynecologic squamous cell carcinomas (vulvar, cervical) at young ages. HPV vaccination is recommended. Gynecologic assessment annually from age 13; Pap smear annually from age 18.

In FA-S (biallelic BRCA1), breast/ovarian tumours have been reported only in female compound-heterozygous patients; homozygous patients have presented with childhood cancers closer to the usual FA pattern. Typical FA females do not get breast/ovarian cancer.

value.name: Xenopus embryonic epidermis foxi1e ionocyte-depletion model
value.genotype: Morpholino knockdown of foxi1e, depleting ionocytes from the embryonic epidermis
value.category: Non-cell-autonomous perturbation of multiciliated cell development
value.description: Frog embryonic skin contains multiciliated, mucus-secreting and foxi1e-dependent ionocyte-like cells. Depleting ionocytes leaves multiciliated cells with fewer and aberrantly beating cilia. The reduced count concerns cilia per cell, not disappearance of the multiciliated cell population. This non-cell-autonomous epithelial perturbation is a surrogate-system finding, not a model of a human PCD genotype.

assertion.description: Produces fewer cilia per multiciliated cell and abnormal ciliary beating by depleting a neighboring epidermal cell type.
assertion.limitations: No PCD gene is involved and no PCD genotype is modelled — the perturbation is of ionocyte development, and the ciliary phenotype is a secondary consequence. Frog embryonic epidermis is a surrogate for airway epithelium rather than the tissue itself, and FOXI1 has not been implicated in human PCD. Treat this as evidence about the cellular architecture that mucociliary function depends on, not as a disease model.

readouts.name: Cilia per multiciliated cell after foxi1e knockdown
readouts.interpretation: Cilia per cell decrease after ionocyte depletion; abnormal beating is also observed. This is not evidence for a reduced number of multiciliated cells.

selected_evidence.snippet: Depletion of ionocytes by foxi1e knockdown has detrimental effects on the development of multiciliated cells, which show fewer and aberrantly beating cilia. These results reveal a newly identified role for ionocytes and suggest that the frog embryonic skin is a model system that is particularly suited to studying the interactions of different cell types in mucociliary, as well as in secretory and transporting, epithelia.

assertion.prompt: Does loss of motile cilia drive airway wall remodeling in human PCD through a direct epithelial-homeostasis route, independently of the infection-inflammation cycle?
assertion.rationale: Conditional IFT88 deletion in adult mice removed airway cilia and produced bronchial remodeling, epithelial hypertrophy and hyperplasia, increased club-cell numbers and airway hyperreactivity without detectable inflammation or an apparent mucus-clearance defect. IFT88 is an intraflagellar-transport gene that also affects non-motile cilia and epithelial differentiation, so the model is not equivalent to a human axonemal PCD genotype. Two node descriptions in this entry already qualify the experiment on those grounds and keep remodeling downstream of chronic infection and inflammation; whether a cilia-autonomous route contributes in human PCD has not been tested.

proposed_experiments.name: Remodeling-versus-inflammation dissociation in early human PCD airway
proposed_experiments.description: In genotype-defined children diagnosed before chronic infection is established, pair bronchial biopsy or brushing histomorphometry (basal and club-cell composition, epithelial hypertrophy, basement-membrane thickening) with airway inflammatory markers and a regional clearance measurement, and test whether structural remodeling is present in airway segments whose inflammatory and clearance measures are unremarkable.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Pre-specify the remodeling indices, the inflammatory and clearance ranges that count as unaffected, and a meaningful effect size, with the participant as the independent unit and adjustment for age, genotype and treatment history.
supporting_outcome: Elevated remodeling indices in segments whose inflammatory markers and clearance sit within the non-PCD range would support a cilia-autonomous contribution in humans.
refuting_outcome: Remodeling that tracks inflammatory burden and clearance failure with no residual component would leave the infection-driven cascade sufficient over the sampled age range.

selected_evidence.snippet: Club cells may be prevented from differentiating into respiratory epithelial cells because of a lack of IFT88 protein that is necessary to form a single nonmotile cilium.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Canonical Axonemal Motile-Cilia Beat-Failure / Mucociliary Clearance Model
assertion.description: Inherited defects in axonemal motors, assembly and regulation impair effective respiratory ciliary beating. Reduced multiciliogenesis and C1d-associated transport dysfunction are parallel upstream routes to impaired mucociliary clearance. Retained secretions favor recurrent infection, neutrophilic inflammation, airway remodeling and heterogeneous obstructive decline. This convergent model does not require complete immotility, abnormal routine TEM, or complete absence of clearance in every patient.
assertion.notes: The complete June OpenScientist report and citation manifest were reassessed in September 2026; the canonical core remains supported. The provider-reported 135-paper corpus is not reconstructable from the 50-PMID sidecar. Valid cilia-number, genotype, reproductive, inflammatory and species qualifications are represented. CCNO residual cilia can retain normal motor proteins, whereas MCIDAS residual cilia lack DNAH5/CCDC39. The report omitted existing genotype-stratified longitudinal work and overstated absence of PCD randomized trials. BESTCILIA reduces exacerbations without separating antimicrobial from immunomodulatory effects; CLEAN-PCD has comparator-specific short-term results. DNAI1 mouse-cell rescue establishes proximal function, while separate 2026 human RCT1100-101/102 conference data did not demonstrate post-treatment ciliary restoration. NOS, sputum-induced M2-like macrophage responses, IFT88 mouse remodeling and infection-induced YTHDF1/DNAH5 regulation remain scoped leads, not universal mutation-intrinsic human pathways. Early-treated infant morbidity does not show early care is ineffective. Full claim and artifact judgments are in the adjacent codex assessment.

assertion.name: Lorlatinib
assertion.description: Third-generation macrocyclic ALK inhibitor, designed to retain potency against the ALK kinase-domain mutations that resist crizotinib and to cross the blood-brain barrier. In the NANT phase 1 trial in relapsed or refractory ALK-driven neuroblastoma the single-agent response rate was 30% in patients under 18 and 67% in those 18 or over, 63% when combined with chemotherapy, with activity across all three neuroblastoma hotspot mutations and in patients who had already received another ALK inhibitor. Reported response rates vary by cohort and by what is counted: 69% in a single-centre adult series and 33% in a French compassionate-use registry, where no patient with MYCN amplification responded. Lorlatinib has replaced crizotinib in the Children's Oncology Group frontline phase 3 trial for ALK-altered high-risk disease. Applicable only to the ALK-altered molecular subset.

effect_modifiers.description: In the French compassionate-use and off-label registry series, response was confined to the MYCN-non-amplified patients: six of ten responded without amplification against none of eight with it. The source states the stratified comparison itself. MYCN amplification is typed BIOMARKER rather than GENOTYPE because it is a somatic tumour feature used to stratify, not a germline or variant genotype of the patient. No interaction test is reported, so interaction_tested is left off.

selected_evidence.snippet: Lorlatinib was optimized to penetrate the blood-brain barrier, leading to improved CNS distribution as well as intracranial responses in patients with NCSLC with brain metastases

assertion.name: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
assertion.description: Langerhans cell histiocytosis and metastatic neuroblastoma can both produce bone lesions of the orbit in children. LCH tends to involve the skull bones, especially the lateral orbital roof, and the orbit is a common site of neuroblastoma bone metastases. At imaging, osseous orbital lesions may appear similar to each other, and LCH, granulocytic sarcoma and neuroblastoma metastases to the orbit are often bilateral. The Euro Histio Net guideline for patients up to 18 years lists neuroblastoma among the possible other conditions in its differential-diagnosis table for LCH involving the orbit. The same table also lists neuroblastoma among the possible other conditions for LCH skin nodules, with mastocytosis, juvenile xanthogranuloma and infant leukemia.
distinguishing_features: LCH tends to involve the skull bones, especially the lateral orbital roof, and produces lytic bone destruction with a sclerotic rim and a large intraorbital soft-tissue mass, whereas neuroblastoma metastases to the orbit cause an aggressive periosteal reaction in the orbital roof or lateral wall.
A definitive diagnosis of LCH requires positive immunostaining of the lesional cells for CD1a and/or CD207 (langerin).

selected_evidence.snippet: Positive immunohistochemistry staining for CD1a and CD207 (langerin) are required for a definitive diagnosis.

assertion.name: Olfactory neuroblastoma
assertion.description: Shares the name and little else. Olfactory neuroblastoma is a sinonasal tumor, most often in the superior nasal cavity at the cribriform plate, that arises from olfactory epithelial globose basal cells and is most common in adults; neuroblastoma is a tumor of the sympathetic nervous system in young children. This entry's MONDO and NCIT classes also contain olfactory neuroblastoma, which its scope note excludes, so the confusion is mainly one of naming and classification rather than at the bedside. On tissue both are small round blue cell tumors, and PHOX2B separates them: all ten olfactory neuroblastomas in one series were negative.
distinguishing_features: A sinonasal site, most often the superior nasal cavity at the cribriform plate, rather than adrenal or paraspinal
Adults rather than young children, with a unimodal peak at about 50 to 60 years
Origin from olfactory epithelial globose basal cells rather than from sympathoadrenal neural crest precursors
PHOX2B-negative; all ten olfactory neuroblastomas in one series were negative by its 5% threshold, while 70 of 76 peripheral neuroblastic tumors were positive

assertion.name: Eflornithine (DFMO) Maintenance Therapy
assertion.description: An oral ornithine decarboxylase inhibitor given as maintenance after front-line therapy, to reduce the risk of relapse rather than to treat active disease. The United States approved indication, granted on 13 December 2023, is for patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who have demonstrated at least a partial response to prior multiagent, multimodality therapy including anti-GD2 immunotherapy; dosing in the pivotal study was oral, twice daily and continued for up to two years. The evidence base is unusual and the record is written around that: approval rested on an externally controlled trial, a single-arm study compared with an external control drawn from a separate cooperative-group trial, and the review describes it as the first oncology approval to rely on that design as its primary clinical data. Against the external control, event-free and overall survival both favoured eflornithine. No randomized trial has tested it in this setting.
assertion.context: High-risk neuroblastoma, post-immunotherapy maintenance in remission
assertion.notes: Three caveats bear on how much this record should be taken to settle, and none of them is visible from the approval alone. First, the reviewers themselves called the missing randomized trial a significant limitation, given reliance on a time-to-event endpoint, and the cited approval summary is quoted for that below rather than only for the indication. Second, the mechanism at the approved dose is open: a 2025 study found that low-dose eflornithine did not extend survival in mouse models and that sensitivity did not track MYCN or ODC1 copy number, which is why the linked pathophysiology node is marked PROVISIONAL rather than ESTABLISHED. Third, two facts relevant to reading the approval are not carried by any publication cached here and are therefore stated without an evidence item: the European Medicines Agency application was withdrawn in July 2025, with a provisional view that effectiveness had not been demonstrated, per the agency's own public medicine page; and the one randomized test of eflornithine in neuroblastoma, an add-on in relapsed or refractory disease (NCT03794349), posted response rates showing no advantage for the eflornithine arm. The registry record's cached body holds only its brief summary, so those figures cannot be quoted as a snippet. Both are recorded here because omitting them would leave "FDA-approved" reading as settled and global.

selected_evidence.snippet: We show that low-dose DFMO does not extend survival in mouse models in vivo nor alter translation biomarkers in vitro.

assertion.name: Hepatoblastoma
assertion.description: A review of infantile hepatic hemangioma lists metastatic neuroblastoma, hepatoblastoma and mesenchymal hamartoma among the primary differential diagnoses of a focal liver lesion in an infant that may be a focal hemangioma, so both tumors are considered when an infant has a focal liver lesion. A pedunculated hepatoblastoma, attached to the liver by a vascular pedicle and presenting as a perihepatic mass, can also be taken for neuroblastoma: in one reported four-month-old infant, a hepatoblastoma in the left upper quadrant was first suspected to be neuroblastoma on abdominal ultrasound. That presentation rests on a single case and establishes a diagnostic pitfall rather than its frequency.
distinguishing_features: In the reported four-month-old, bone marrow aspiration and 24-hour urinary VMA and HVA were negative for neuroblastoma; with CT showing nutrient vessels entering the mass from the left hepatic vein, coarse calcification and its enhancement pattern, pedunculated hepatoblastoma was suggested, serum AFP was above 100,000 ng/ml (the report's normal range is 5-109), and percutaneous biopsy confirmed hepatoblastoma.

The case report's authors conclude that pedunculated hepatoblastoma should be considered when a perihepatic mass in a child can be confused with other upper abdominal masses such as an adrenal mass, and that the vascular pedicle should then be looked for on imaging and the AFP check kept in mind.

assertion.name: Eflornithine (DFMO) Maintenance Therapy
assertion.description: An oral ornithine decarboxylase inhibitor given as maintenance after front-line therapy, to reduce the risk of relapse rather than to treat active disease. The United States approved indication, granted on 13 December 2023, is for patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who have demonstrated at least a partial response to prior multiagent, multimodality therapy including anti-GD2 immunotherapy; dosing in the pivotal study was oral, twice daily and continued for up to two years. The evidence base is unusual and the record is written around that: approval rested on an externally controlled trial, a single-arm study compared with an external control drawn from a separate cooperative-group trial, and the review describes it as the first oncology approval to rely on that design as its primary clinical data. Against the external control, event-free and overall survival both favoured eflornithine. No randomized trial has tested it in this setting.
assertion.context: High-risk neuroblastoma, post-immunotherapy maintenance in remission
assertion.notes: Three caveats bear on how much this record should be taken to settle, and none of them is visible from the approval alone. First, the reviewers themselves called the missing randomized trial a significant limitation, given reliance on a time-to-event endpoint, and the cited approval summary is quoted for that below rather than only for the indication. Second, the mechanism at the approved dose is open: a 2025 study found that low-dose eflornithine did not extend survival in mouse models and that sensitivity did not track MYCN or ODC1 copy number, which is why the linked pathophysiology node is marked PROVISIONAL rather than ESTABLISHED. Third, two facts relevant to reading the approval are not carried by any publication cached here and are therefore stated without an evidence item: the European Medicines Agency application was withdrawn in July 2025, with a provisional view that effectiveness had not been demonstrated, per the agency's own public medicine page; and the one randomized test of eflornithine in neuroblastoma, an add-on in relapsed or refractory disease (NCT03794349), posted response rates showing no advantage for the eflornithine arm. The registry record's cached body holds only its brief summary, so those figures cannot be quoted as a snippet. Both are recorded here because omitting them would leave "FDA-approved" reading as settled and global.

assertion.prompt: How do zygosity, affected cell lineage and deletion timing influence the relevance of mouse and stem-cell BRPF1 models to variable human heterozygous disease?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Impaired Hematopoietic Stem and Progenitor Cell Maintenance
assertion.rationale: Complete global, early forebrain and hematopoietic loss can cause lethal mouse phenotypes, whereas postnatal CaMKIIa-Cre conditional mice survive and have selective physiological and behavioral effects. Emx1-lineage conditional heterozygotes match human zygosity only within the targeted lineage, not throughout the organism. Human expressivity varies, including a reported individual with normal intellectual development; these observations do not establish normal life expectancy. Human callosal abnormalities are uncommon. Anemia and thrombocytopenia have been reported in a family and in additional individuals in the 2025 cohort, without demonstrating the severe stem-cell failure mechanism of the homozygous hematopoietic mouse model. Global null embryos also have placental and vascular defects with cranial neural tube failure. Zebrafish pharyngeal homeotic transformations establish a developmental role, but have no demonstrated equivalent in human heterozygous craniofacial dysmorphism.

proposed_experiments.name: BRPF1 zygosity-matched allelic series in human iPSC-derived cortical neurons and organoids
proposed_experiments.description: In an isogenic human iPSC background, build a BRPF1 allelic series (heterozygous null, heterozygous patient truncating and missense alleles, homozygous null) and differentiate to cortical neurons and forebrain organoids. Read out H3K23 acetylation and propionylation, chromatin accessibility, intermediate-progenitor (TBR2) abundance, dendritic arborization, and excitatory and inhibitory synaptic physiology. This directly tests whether the heterozygous human state reproduces the null-allele mouse phenotypes and, if so, at what magnitude.

assertion.prompt: In Wilson disease liver, is the iron-dependent component of injury true ferroptosis, or is it non-specific iron-catalyzed oxidative damage layered onto copper-driven lipid peroxidation?
assertion.rationale: The iron-lowering experiments that motivate this node were performed in LEC rats decades before ferroptosis assays existed, and the human data measure glutathione depletion and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances, which are generic oxidative-stress endpoints rather than ferroptosis markers. Copper is itself a stronger pro-oxidant and thiol-binding agent than iron in liver fractions, so the same readouts are expected from copper alone. Without a ferroptosis-specific rescue and GPX4 or ACSL4 readouts in an ATP7B-deficient system, this entry cannot say whether ferroptosis is a distinct injury pathway here or a relabelling of copper-driven oxidative damage.

assertion.name: Impaired Synaptic Transmission and Plasticity
assertion.description: Where the affected theme is synaptic, the immediate cellular consequence is a defect in excitatory neurotransmission or in the activity-dependent changes that encode experience. GRIK2 loss removes a kainate-receptor subunit from the excitatory synapse with electrophysiologically confirmed loss of function; PRSS12/neurotrypsin loss removes a protease acting at the presynaptic membrane lining the synaptic cleft, where its proteolysis is required for normal synaptic function; MED23 loss blocks JUN/FOS immediate-early-gene induction, the transcriptional arm of activity-dependent plasticity; MBOAT7 loss alters the arachidonoyl phosphatidylinositol pool from which synaptic signalling lipids derive; and CC2D1A loss releases PDE4D hyperactivity, depleting hippocampal cAMP and reducing CREB signalling. The resulting deficit is in the machinery of learning and memory rather than in gross brain structure - which is precisely why the phenotype is cognitive and non-syndromic.

assertion.prompt: What fraction of all intellectual disability is attributable to autosomal recessive NON-SYNDROMIC gene defects, in consanguineous and in outbred populations?
assertion.rationale: Every published figure is either the all-cause intellectual disability prevalence (about 1%), a whole-class share (about 10% of affected children in an outbred population, syndromic and non-syndromic combined), or a solve rate within a clinic-ascertained multiplex consanguineous cohort (37-58%). None is a population estimate for the non-syndromic recessive class. Solve rates are inflated by multiplex ascertainment - families were selected for having two or more affected offspring, which enriches for recessive inheritance by construction - and are further confounded by cohorts that mix syndromic and non-syndromic cases; in one large consanguineous series 92% of families had additional features beyond intellectual disability. Without a population-based denominator the burden of this class, and therefore the case for carrier-screening programmes, cannot be quantified.

proposed_experiments.name: Unselected population-based sequencing of intellectual disability in a high-consanguinity setting
proposed_experiments.description: Ascertain intellectual disability cases from a defined population rather than from genetics clinics, apply exome or genome sequencing to all, and have a clinical geneticist classify each case as syndromic or non-syndromic blinded to the genotype. This yields the first genuine population numerator and denominator for the non-syndromic recessive class, and simultaneously measures the size of the multiplex ascertainment inflation affecting existing estimates.

proposed_experiments.description: Re-analyse published large consanguineous cohorts stratifying solve rate by number of affected siblings and by syndromic status, to estimate and correct the ascertainment inflation in the headline yields and derive a bias-adjusted class share.

assertion.prompt: Do the rodent models used for AR-NSID genes report on human intellectual disability, given that the rescued readouts are sex-restricted rodent memory assays and that a key dosage mechanism (parent-of-origin bias) is established only in mouse brain?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Impaired Cortical Circuit Formation and Connectivity
assertion.rationale: Evidence exists in the models; what is open is whether it transfers. Three specific mismatches are documented rather than hypothetical. First, intellectual disability is a construct (IQ plus adaptive functioning) with no animal equivalent, so every model readout is a proxy - Drosophila short-term memory for NSUN2, mouse spatial and social memory for CC2D1A and TRAPPC9. Second, the one pharmacological rescue in the class is MALE-SPECIFIC: the PDE4D signalling deficit is absent in Cc2d1a-deficient female mice and the inhibitor has no effect in them, so a therapy developed on this model could fail in half of patients for reasons the model cannot reveal. Third, the parent-of-origin dosage mechanism for Trappc9 is established in mouse brain, and its human correlate rests on a single child with increased food intake - a metabolic rather than cognitive readout at n=1. This is a HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH rather than a KNOWLEDGE_GAP because in each case the model data are solid and it is their translational validity that is uncertain.

A negative result would indicate the male-specific mouse mechanism does not transfer.

assertion.name: MRT78
assertion.description: Biallelic loss-of-function WDR11 variants in six patients from three independent families, with intellectual disability, microcephaly and short stature. The founding report's own argument is that this recessive entity is clinically distinct from the dominantly inherited WDR11 missense phenotype of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, which this knowledge base curates separately as a subtype of Kallmann syndrome; that distinctness is why the gene earns a row here as well as there. The closest of the six subtypes added in this pass to the syndromic boundary, and it is kept on the non-obligate reading: individual patients carry further findings, among them ophthalmological, skeletal, auditory and pigmentary ones, but these differ between individuals rather than forming a consistent gestalt, and the report's own core-feature set is the cognitive phenotype with microcephaly and mild short stature. Microcephaly is not a disqualifier for this class.

assertion.hypothesis_label: The non-syndromic label reflects depth of phenotyping and cohort size rather than a mechanistically distinct disease class
assertion.description: Under this model AR-NSID is the leading edge of recessive gene discovery rather than a separate biological entity: a gene-disease pair is called non-syndromic while it rests on one or two consanguineous pedigrees and a routine dysmorphology examination, and migrates into a named syndrome once enough patients accumulate to reveal a gestalt. The prediction is that MRT-series entities will be progressively reclassified, and several already have been. Within this entry, MRT5/NSUN2 was reported with accompanying facial dysmorphism and the discovering authors themselves raised the possibility of a syndromic form; MRT15/MAN1B1 was reported with a mixed cohort (three strictly non-syndromic families plus one with additional features) and now carries the eponymous MONDO label "Rafiq syndrome"; and ADAT3 - initially characterised as cognitive impairment with strabismus - became "an important recognizable cause of intellectual disability in Arabia" with dysmorphic features once a second cohort was described. The competing, not mutually exclusive model is that a genuine subset of genes has sufficiently brain-restricted consequence that isolated cognitive impairment is the real phenotype; TUSC3 is the strongest case, since N-glycosylation defects usually produce florid multisystem disease yet TUSC3 loss does not. Distinguishing the two requires prospective deep phenotyping of MRT-series cohorts, which has not been done.

assertion.prompt: Mutant TDP-43 knock-in mice develop motor axon degeneration and motor-neuron death with neither nuclear TDP-43 clearance nor TDP-43 aggregates. Does that mean cytoplasmic aggregation and nuclear depletion are also dispensable in human ALS, where both are near-universal findings?
assertion.rationale: TDP-43 Q331K and M337V mice expressed at endogenous levels develop age-dependent, mutant-dependent motor axon degeneration and lower motor neuron death without loss of nuclear TDP-43, without aggregates, and without insoluble TDP-43, while showing both loss and gain of splicing function at selected RNA targets. Taken literally, that dissociates degeneration from the two features this entry treats as the defining lesion of TDP-43 proteinopathy. The mismatch is that the finding is a sufficiency result in an engineered mutant model, whereas ~97% of human ALS — the great majority of it sporadic and not TARDBP-mutant — does show nuclear clearance and phosphorylated cytoplasmic inclusions. The model therefore establishes that an ALS-linked mutant can kill motor neurons through altered splicing alone; it does not establish the temporal position, toxicity, or possible protective role of aggregates in sporadic human disease, and it should not be read as demonstrating that human TDP-43 aggregation is merely a late-stage marker. Resolving this determines whether therapy should target aggregate clearance, TDP-43 localization, or the RNA-processing changes directly.

proposed_experiments.name: Aggregation- and localization-separated TDP-43 toxicity in human motor neurons
proposed_experiments.description: In isogenic human iPSC-derived motor neurons, express TDP-43 variants engineered to separate the three features: aggregation-incompetent mutants that retain altered splicing, nuclear-retained mutants, and mutants that aggregate without changing splicing. Compare survival, axonal integrity and cryptic-splicing burden across arms, and benchmark the resulting splicing signatures against nuclear-cleared versus nuclear-preserved motor neurons sampled from sporadic ALS postmortem tissue.

experiment_type.preferred_term: isogenic human iPSC motor-neuron structure-function dissociation experiment

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Motor-neuron death in the aggregation-incompetent arm, with a splicing signature matching nuclear-cleared human ALS motor neurons, would extend the mouse result to human cells and argue that RNA misprocessing rather than aggregation is the actionable lesion; survival in that arm together with death in the aggregating arm would confine the mouse finding to mutant-driven disease and keep aggregate species as a human therapeutic target.

selected_evidence.snippet: TDP-43 was identified as a primary component of ubiquitinated and hyper-phosphorylated cytosolic aggregates observed from post-mortem tissue of patients with ALS

assertion.prompt: Can chlorpromazine, or another phenothiazine antipsychotic, be repurposed as a disease-modifying ALS therapy on the strength of lysosomal TPC2 agonism, TFEB-driven autophagy induction and enhanced TDP-43 aggregate clearance — or does the dopaminergic pharmacology that defines the class cancel any proteostatic benefit at exposures a person with ALS could tolerate?
assertion.rationale:
Three independent lines converge on the phenothiazine scaffold as a proteostasis-directed ALS lead. An unbiased neuronal autophagy-inducer screen returned two phenothiazine antipsychotics as its top hits and showed that autophagy induction accelerates TDP-43 turnover and improves survival in human stem-cell-derived neurons; thioridazine cleared TDP-43 aggregates, restored TDP-43 splicing function and rescued locomotion in Drosophila; and chlorpromazine itself was shown to open the lysosomal TPC2 channel in NSC-34 motor neurons, driving Ca2+-dependent TFEB translocation and protecting against the ALS/PDC neurotoxin L-BMAA, with TPC2 knockdown reverting the protection. Each of those is a different route to the same node this discussion attaches to, and none has been tested in a mammalian ALS model.
The hypothesis is nevertheless not simply untested — it is tested by proxy, and the proxies failed. Methylene blue shares the tricyclic phenothiazine-type core, reduced TDP-43 aggregates in cells, and then conferred no benefit in SOD1-G93A or TDP-43-G348C mice. Pimozide, a neuroleptic selected by the same simple-organism screening logic, reached a short randomized ALS trial with apparent target engagement at the neuromuscular junction, and chronic dosing then worsened motor performance in two ALS mouse models and shortened SOD1-G93A survival. Clozapine delayed decline at low dose and accelerated paralysis and death at high dose in the same model. So the open question is not whether phenothiazines induce autophagy in motor neurons — they do — but whether a therapeutic window exists between the concentration that engages TPC2/TFEB and the concentration at which D2 blockade produces rigidity, sedation and dysphagia in a population whose leading cause of death is respiratory and bulbar failure.
The epidemiological premise that originally motivated neuroleptic repurposing in ALS — that ALS is strikingly rare among people with schizophrenia — should not be carried forward. It was a clinical impression, and the ALS/schizophrenia genetic correlation is positive (14.3%), predicting a modest increase rather than a decrease in comorbidity.
A closer look at TPC2 itself narrows the hypothesis further, and not in its favour. TPC2's ion selectivity is set by which ligand opens it: a NAADP-mimetic evokes non-selective cation currents and robust Ca2+ signals, a PI(3,5)P2-mimetic evokes Na+-selective currents and weaker ones, and the two drive lysosomal pH and exocytosis in opposite directions. The chlorpromazine result sits squarely on the NAADP arm — the paper benchmarks the chlorpromazine-evoked current against NAADP and its mimetic TPC2-A1-N, and blocks it with trans-Ned-19. That is the arm with no in vivo efficacy precedent anywhere: the lysosomal-storage rescue that put TPC2 on the map used the PI(3,5)P2-mimetic TPC2-A1-P throughout, including in its MLIV mouse, and in LRRK2 Parkinson's models the beneficial agonist was one biased to reduce Ca2+ permeability, with TPC2 itself the pathogenic element. So the chain this hypothesis proposes runs through the one mode of the one channel for which no animal has yet been shown to benefit.
Two consequences for the experiments below. First, the window study should read out the PI(3,5)P2-biased mode as well, because if substrate clearance in motor neurons tracks that mode instead, the useful compound is a biased TPC2 agonist and not an antipsychotic. Second, the obvious alternative of blocking TPC2 instead — which is neuroprotective in stroke and in LRRK2 models, and is the better-developed arm pharmacologically — carries a motor-neuron-specific liability that those indications do not: trans-Ned-19, the same antagonist, attenuates Ca2+ transients in zebrafish caudal primary motor neurons and inhibits their axon extension. In a motor-neuron disease the better-developed arm of TPC2 pharmacology acts against the arm of TPC2 biology that motor neurons demonstrably need. See kb/modules/lysosomal_substrate_accumulation.yaml (controversy_tpc2_direction_of_modulation) for the direction question in general.

proposed_experiments.name: Phenothiazine TPC2/TFEB engagement versus tolerated CNS exposure in ALS
proposed_experiments.description: Establish, for chlorpromazine and for the screen-derived phenothiazines fluphenazine and methotrimeprazine, the free concentration required in human iPSC-derived motor neurons to produce TPC2-dependent TFEB nuclear translocation and measurable TDP-43 clearance, then compare it against free CSF and spinal-cord concentrations achieved in wild-type and SOD1-G93A mice at doses below the threshold for hindlimb rigidity and catalepsy. Include a TPC2-null arm to confirm that clearance in motor neurons is channel-dependent rather than a general lysosomotropic effect of the cationic amphiphilic scaffold.

experiment_type.preferred_term: pharmacodynamic-pharmacokinetic window study in iPSC motor neurons and mouse CNS

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: A viable window requires the TFEB/TDP-43-clearance EC50 to sit below the free CNS concentration reached at a non-cataleptic dose, with at least a severalfold margin. If engagement demands concentrations only reached at doses producing extrapyramidal signs, the repurposing hypothesis should be abandoned for the marketed antipsychotics and redirected to TPC2 agonists without dopamine-receptor affinity.
supporting_outcome: TPC2-dependent TFEB translocation and TDP-43 clearance at free concentrations several-fold below those producing catalepsy or hindlimb rigidity in mice.
refuting_outcome: Engagement only at concentrations at or above the motor-toxicity threshold, or clearance that persists in TPC2-null motor neurons and is therefore an off-target lysosomotropic effect.

proposed_experiments.name: Dose-ranging chlorpromazine survival study in TDP-43 and SOD1 ALS mice
proposed_experiments.description: Run chlorpromazine at a minimum of three doses spanning the window identified above in both TDP-43-A315T and SOD1-G93A mice, powered for survival and with prespecified neuromuscular-junction innervation, insoluble TDP-43, misfolded SOD1 and spinal-cord LC3-II/p62 endpoints. Two models and a dose range are both required: the pimozide study found opposite-signed effects from the short human trial, and the clozapine study found opposite-signed effects between low and high dose within one model, so a single-dose single-model result cannot settle this.

experiment_type.preferred_term: dose-ranging survival study in two transgenic ALS mouse models

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Chlorpromazine should extend survival or preserve neuromuscular-junction innervation in at least one model at a dose whose autophagic target engagement is confirmed in the same spinal cords. Worsened motor performance, shortened survival, or increased insoluble TDP-43 or misfolded SOD1 at any dose — the pimozide result — closes the hypothesis for chlorpromazine.
supporting_outcome: Survival extension or preserved neuromuscular-junction innervation at a dose with confirmed spinal-cord autophagy induction.
refuting_outcome: Worsened motor performance, shortened survival, or increased insoluble TDP-43 or misfolded SOD1 at any tested dose.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Canonical Motor Neuron Proteostatic Failure Model
assertion.description: Progressive upper and lower motor neuron degeneration in ALS is the convergent endpoint of multiple genetic and sporadic insults that ultimately cause proteostatic failure. Key drivers include cytoplasmic mislocalization and aggregation of TDP-43 (in >97% of cases), C9orf72 hexanucleotide repeat expansion–derived dipeptide repeats and RNA foci, SOD1 misfolding, FUS/EWSR1 phase-separation defects, impaired autophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction, axonal transport failure, and neuroinflammation. Selective vulnerability of cortical layer-5 Betz cells and spinal alpha motor neurons leads to progressive muscle denervation, weakness, atrophy, and ultimately respiratory failure. Antisense-oligonucleotide therapy targeting SOD1 (tofersen) provides the strongest interventional validation of the SOD1 genetic-pathogenetic axis of this canonical multi-hit model, although that validation rests on target engagement and biomarker lowering rather than on a positive randomized clinical endpoint. The C9orf72 ASO program (BIIB078) was discontinued after a Phase 1 study that showed neither neurofilament reduction nor clinical benefit, indicating that lowering sense-strand repeat RNA alone is insufficient; that single negative program does not by itself establish which of the competing C9orf72 mechanisms — antisense-strand RNA toxicity, dipeptide-repeat proteins, or haploinsufficiency — dominates.
assertion.notes: Retained as CANONICAL. The 2026 openscientist hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Amyotrophic_Lateral_Sclerosis/canonical_motor_neuron_proteostatic_failure_model) confirms convergent proteostatic failure as the unifying ALS mechanism: TDP-43 proteinopathy in ~97% of cases, SOD1 misfolding, C9orf72 RNA foci and DPRs, FUS phase-separation defects, impaired autophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction, axonal transport failure, and neuroinflammation all converge on motor-neuron degeneration. Tofersen (SOD1 ASO) approval provides the strongest causal validation of the genetic-pathogenetic axes. Four qualifications: (1) the C9orf72-ASO program (BIIB078; Phase 1 discontinued) showed insufficient clinical efficacy — lowering sense-strand repeat RNA does not consistently translate to motor preservation. The 2026 openscientist report reads that failure as evidence that DPR-mediated toxicity dominates; the assessment (assessments/openscientist-assessment-by-codex.yaml, claim c9orf72-failure-mechanism) rejects that inference, since one ASO at one dose range and exposure period cannot separate incomplete target engagement, treatment timing, antisense-strand transcripts, DPR toxicity, haploinsufficiency, or persistent TDP-43 pathology. assertion.hypothesis_label: Canonical Motor Neuron Proteostatic Failure Model
assertion.description: Progressive upper and lower motor neuron degeneration in ALS is the convergent endpoint of multiple genetic and sporadic insults that ultimately cause proteostatic failure. Key drivers include cytoplasmic mislocalization and aggregation of TDP-43 (in >97% of cases), C9orf72 hexanucleotide repeat expansion–derived dipeptide repeats and RNA foci, SOD1 misfolding, FUS/EWSR1 phase-separation defects, impaired autophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction, axonal transport failure, and neuroinflammation. Selective vulnerability of cortical layer-5 Betz cells and spinal alpha motor neurons leads to progressive muscle denervation, weakness, atrophy, and ultimately respiratory failure. Antisense-oligonucleotide therapy targeting SOD1 (tofersen) provides the strongest interventional validation of the SOD1 genetic-pathogenetic axis of this canonical multi-hit model, although that validation rests on target engagement and biomarker lowering rather than on a positive randomized clinical endpoint. The C9orf72 ASO program (BIIB078) was discontinued after a Phase 1 study that showed neither neurofilament reduction nor clinical benefit, indicating that lowering sense-strand repeat RNA alone is insufficient; that single negative program does not by itself establish which of the competing C9orf72 mechanisms — antisense-strand RNA toxicity, dipeptide-repeat proteins, or haploinsufficiency — dominates.
assertion.notes: Retained as CANONICAL. The 2026 openscientist hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Amyotrophic_Lateral_Sclerosis/canonical_motor_neuron_proteostatic_failure_model) confirms convergent proteostatic failure as the unifying ALS mechanism: TDP-43 proteinopathy in ~97% of cases, SOD1 misfolding, C9orf72 RNA foci and DPRs, FUS phase-separation defects, impaired autophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction, axonal transport failure, and neuroinflammation all converge on motor-neuron degeneration. (4) The tofersen evidence is target-engagement- and biomarker-led: VALOR's prespecified 28-week ALSFRS-R primary endpoint and its clinical secondary endpoints did not separate from placebo, and the longer-term early-start versus delayed-start advantage comes from an open-label extension with substantial attrition, so it is not a blinded randomized efficacy comparison.

value.name: Equine motor neuron disease (vitamin E-deficient horse)
value.genotype: acquired (vitamin E deficiency / chronic oxidative stress)
value.description: Equine motor neuron disease (EMND) is a naturally occurring, acquired lower motor neuron disease of adult horses linked to chronic vitamin E deficiency and oxidative stress, arising in horses stabled without access to pasture. Clinical signs include progressive weight loss, muscle fasciculations, constant weight shifting in the rear limbs, abnormally low head carriage, and excessive recumbency. Pathological findings include type 1 muscle fibre atrophy and lipopigment accumulation in spinal cord capillary endothelium. Unlike classic ALS, which requires combined upper and lower motor neuron degeneration, EMND involves predominantly lower motor neurons (no upper motor neuron involvement), limiting direct phenotypic equivalence to human ALS.

assertion.description: Chronic vitamin E deficiency is proposed to produce a sustained oxidative insult to motor neurons, giving a naturally occurring model of the oxidative stress node that is separable from any genetic lesion.
assertion.limitations: The oxidative insult here is nutritional; it is a model of oxidative stress as a sufficient cause of motor neuron injury, not of the SOD1- or TDP-43-driven oxidative stress seen in human ALS. The oxidative mechanism is itself inferred: the cited studies support it with a histological marker (endothelial lipopigment), case-control dietary risk factors, and uncontrolled improvement after pasture access, and frame it as a hypothesis rather than as a measured oxidative-damage readout.

readouts.name: Spinal cord capillary endothelial lipopigment accumulation
readouts.description: Lipopigment deposition in spinal cord capillary endothelium at post mortem, the histological marker the authors read as oxidative injury.
readouts.interpretation: Present in all cases, and the basis on which the authors classify EMND as an oxidative disease.

readouts.name: Clinical status after pasture access and vitamin E supplementation
readouts.description: Observational rescue arm: five affected horses were followed for 9 months to over 2 years after onset with pasture access, two also receiving supplemental vitamin E.
readouts.interpretation: Improvement on removal of the oxidative insult is the strongest evidence that the deficiency is driving the node rather than accompanying it. It is observational and uncontrolled, and only the more acutely affected horses improved.

selected_evidence.snippet: The relationship of specific nutritional factors to EMND supports the hypothesis that a deficiency of vitamin E contributes to the disease.

assertion.rationale: The remaining clinical gaps have distinct evidence limitations. GeneReviews supports migraine as a possible trigger of stroke-like episodes, now represented in that direction; it does not establish the cause of migraine or a reverse cortical-injury-to-migraine relation. Short stature and learning disability are documented clinically, but the reviewed sources do not identify a phenotype-specific causal relation from the curated mechanisms; learning disability is not interchangeable with acquired dementia. The m.3243A>G cohort documents MELAS/PEO overlap without establishing the causal sequence from generalized myopathy to extraocular dysfunction. The ptosis case provides occurrence evidence, including a prior myasthenia diagnosis, without establishing eyelid-muscle pathogenesis. Broad conduction abnormalities, right bundle branch block, and Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome are documented, but the reviewed sources do not establish their causal route from the curated myocardial remodeling mechanism or explain how mitochondrial dysfunction produces an accessory conduction pathway. The anemia cohort explicitly leaves dietary and other contributors unresolved. The imaging study documents cerebellar atrophy and basal ganglia calcification but does not establish their causal route from the cortical stroke-like lesion mechanism. Its suggestion of dystrophic calcification does not identify the initiating injury. Lactate, ragged-red fibers, and focal epileptiform EEG discharges are linked separately as observational readouts. GeneReviews documents ataxia without assigning it to the cortical injury mechanism or establishing that the imaged cerebellar atrophy causes it. The cardiac review supports a qualified remodeling-to-arrhythmia relation, now represented, but the right bundle branch block case is not causally assigned to that remodeling route by the observational cohort. These gaps concern causal attribution, not a requirement to identify every intermediate step.

assertion.prompt: Which cardiac findings reported across m.3243A>G carriers can be assigned specifically to clinically defined MELAS?
assertion.rationale: The systematic cardiac review pools m.3243A>G carriers with MELAS, MIDD, MERRF, Leigh syndrome, and MELAS/KSS overlap. It reports left and right bundle branch block, supraventricular and ventricular arrhythmias, sinus tachycardia, atrial fibrillation, nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, and sudden cardiac death. Its myocardial spectrum includes thickening, hypertrophic and dilated cardiomyopathy, noncompaction, fibrosis, systolic dysfunction, heart failure, and arterial hypertension; myocardial abnormalities are reported more often than arrhythmias or conduction defects. These observations remain relevant to cardiac assessment, but the review abstract does not assign each manifestation or its frequency to a MELAS subgroup. GeneReviews independently supports MELAS cardiomyopathy, broad conduction abnormalities, and WPW, and recommends ECG and echocardiographic surveillance. Independent clinical MELAS evidence does establish right bundle branch block in a selected 11-patient cohort and non-sustained atrial tachycardia in a case report; these are now represented using those sources. The clinical review also describes atrial fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia and proposes conduction-pathway mitochondrial dysfunction, while the cardiac cohort review describes a remodeling-to-rhythm-disorder route. Sudden cardiac death and left bundle branch block remain carrier-spectrum observations here because the reviewed primary reports do not establish those outcomes in their MELAS patients. Prophylactic device recommendations are not evidence that a sudden-death event occurred.

assertion.prompt: Why does one variant, m.3243A>G, produce MELAS in some carriers, MIDD or isolated deafness in others, and nothing at all in a further group?
assertion.rationale:
Only about 10% of m.3243A>G carriers in a systematically phenotyped cohort had classical MELAS, while 30% had MIDD, 28% had a combination fitting no recognized syndrome, and 9% were asymptomatic. Heteroplasmy level is the conventional explanation, but measured heteroplasmy explains far less than it is credited with: it did not correlate with disease severity in leukocytes or urinary epithelial cells, and it did not correlate with the grade of retinal dystrophy either. Tissue-specific segregation, nuclear genetic background, mtDNA copy number, and age are all candidate modifiers, and none has been shown to account for the variance. This is what makes genetic counselling and prognosis in m.3243A>G families so weak.
Four public datasets attached here attack the gap from different angles and are worth reading against each other. GSE202747 measures heteroplasmy per cell in a human MELAS tissue and finds it partitions by developmental lineage rather than randomly, which would make any single bulk measurement a poor proxy. GSE56158 varies heteroplasmy experimentally in one nuclear background and finds sharp transcriptional transitions rather than a gradient, offering a mechanism by which a continuous variable yields named syndromes. GSE129091 compares low against high load directly on the MELAS-versus-MIDD axis and reports that the two look alike transcriptionally while differing functionally. GSE85549 moves the question from heteroplasmy to allele, comparing the MELAS m.3243A>G lesion against the myopathy-causing m.3302A>G in the same gene. MSV000088237 extends the allele question outside MT-TL1 entirely, profiling fibroblasts from a patient with the complex I subunit variant m.14453G>A. GSE1462 is the only one that holds genotype constant and varies phenotype in patients - four PEO against four MELAS, all m.3243A>G, all muscle - and its authors read the difference as support for nuclear background as the modifier. That is the right experimental design for this gap, at a sample size and on a 2005 platform that cannot settle it.

assertion.description: Biallelic CFTR pathogenic variants impair the cyclic-AMP-regulated apical anion channel that exports chloride and bicarbonate at epithelial surfaces. Loss of CFTR-mediated anion secretion (and secondary hyperabsorption of sodium and water) produces dehydrated, acidic, viscous airway surface liquid and pancreatic/biliary secretions. The resulting impaired mucociliary clearance, chronic bacterial airway infection, and obstructive secretions drive the progressive bronchiectatic lung disease, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, hepatobiliary disease, elevated sweat chloride, and male infertility (CBAVD) characteristic of cystic fibrosis. CFTR modulator therapies (correctors/potentiators, exemplified by elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor) that restore residual CFTR activity provide direct interventional validation of this canonical pathway.
assertion.notes: Retained as CANONICAL following independent assessment of the 2026 OpenScientist hypothesis-search report (see kb/hypotheses/Cystic_Fibrosis/canonical_cftr_loss_of_function_model/assessments/openscientist-assessment-by-codex.md; reconciliation tracked in issue #7325). The core mechanism is well supported by convergent evidence: newborn CF-pig airway-surface-liquid acidification impairs bacterial killing before infection or inflammation, and randomized/registry CFTR-modulator trials (ETI: ppFEV1 +9.9 across 11,151 registry patients) provide direct human interventional validation. Several report-level claims required narrowing rather than verbatim promotion: (1) as of the 2013 CFTR2 analysis, few of the nearly 2,000 then-reported CFTR variants had empirical evidence of disease causation, so an unqualified ">2,000 disease-causing variants" count conflates reported with clinically classified variants; CFTR2 has interpreted substantially more variants since, so any exact count must be dated to its source snapshot rather than asserted in the present tense; (2) bicarbonate secretion has been shown to be rate-limiting for host defense in mixed porcine airway epithelia and cell-culture systems, but this does not establish bicarbonate as the universal rate-limiting determinant over chloride across all human tissues and genotypes; (3) human monocyte-derived macrophages show direct CFTR-dependent defects, but a cited CFTR-depleted zebrafish neutrophil-recruitment finding traced the effect to epithelial oxidative signaling rather than immune-cell-autonomous CFTR dysfunction, so the two should not be conflated as one parallel immune mechanism; (4) residual airway inflammation and molecular abnormalities persisting after highly effective modulator therapy reflect incomplete correction of CFTR function rather than proof that inflammation becomes independent of ongoing CFTR dysfunction; and (5) next-generation vanzacaftor evidence of differential response in two previously unresponsive genotypes is from intestinal organoids, not yet a demonstrated clinical rescue.

selected_evidence.snippet: Few of the almost 2,000 variants in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator gene CFTR have empirical evidence that they cause cystic fibrosis.

assertion.prompt: How much of cystic fibrosis lung disease is attributable to immune-cell-autonomous CFTR dysfunction, independently of the epithelial surface defect?
assertion.rationale: Macrophage CFTR is measurable, modulator-responsive, and associated with reduced phagocytosis, intracellular killing and efferocytosis, and ENaC is overexpressed in cystic fibrosis immune cells in a way that CFTR inhibition reproduces in non-cystic-fibrosis cells. All of this is ex vivo work on blood-derived cells. No study separates the immune contribution from the epithelial one in vivo, so the weight of this arm in human airway disease is unknown, and it cannot be assumed to hold for every immune lineage. A frequently cited zebrafish result does not close the gap either: those larvae were globally CFTR-depleted, and the excess neutrophil recruitment was traced to an epithelial oxidative response rather than to an immune-cell-autonomous defect. Resolving this determines whether immune-directed therapy, such as ENaC modulation in macrophages, is worth pursuing alongside CFTR modulators.

proposed_experiments.name: Reciprocal bone-marrow chimeras between CFTR-null and wild-type animals
proposed_experiments.description: Transplant wild-type marrow into CFTR-null recipients and CFTR-null marrow into wild-type recipients in an animal model that develops airway disease, then compare bacterial burden, neutrophilic inflammation and airway histopathology against the two unmanipulated genotypes.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: An intermediate phenotype in both chimera directions would quantify a real immune-cell-autonomous contribution; a phenotype that tracks recipient airway genotype alone would place the mechanism entirely in the epithelium.
supporting_outcome: Wild-type marrow reducing disease in CFTR-null recipients, and CFTR-null marrow producing inflammation in wild-type recipients, would establish an immune-cell-autonomous contribution and give its approximate size.
refuting_outcome: Disease severity determined solely by the recipient airway genotype, with no effect of donor marrow genotype, would show the macrophage defect to be a downstream marker rather than an independent driver.

selected_evidence.snippet: Baseline expression of ENaC in human CF MDMs, lymphocytes, and granulocytes was increased at both the transcript and protein level relative to non-CF controls and persisted after exposure to bacteria.

assertion.prompt: Why does airway inflammation persist after highly effective CFTR modulator therapy, and is any part of it genuinely independent of ongoing CFTR dysfunction?
assertion.rationale: Sputum proteomes and cytokine profiles improve substantially on elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor but remain distinct from healthy controls, and residual oxidative stress and infection persist at levels comparable to non-cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis. In vitro, restoring roughly 60% of CFTR function does not normalize the lipid imbalance or the basal inflammatory cytokine profile of cystic fibrosis bronchial epithelium. What these observations establish is incomplete normalization, not independence from CFTR. Partial target restoration, irreversible structural injury, persistent infection and microbiome disruption, late treatment initiation, and cell-type-specific drug exposure are all still viable explanations, and the published data do not separate them. The distinction matters for therapy: a self-sustaining cascade would justify adjunct anti-inflammatory treatment on top of modulators, whereas incomplete correction argues for deeper or earlier CFTR restoration.

proposed_experiments.name: Longitudinal airway multi-omics in infant-initiated versus late-initiated modulator therapy
proposed_experiments.description: Follow two prospective cohorts starting elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor, one before six months of age and one after established structural lung disease, with serial airway proteomics, cytokines, microbiome sequencing and imaging, against matched controls without cystic fibrosis.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Convergence of the infant-initiated cohort on the control airway proteome and microbiome would attribute the residual signature to accumulated injury and timing; persistence of an inflammatory signature in that cohort despite equivalent restored CFTR function would support a component that no longer depends on ongoing CFTR dysfunction.
supporting_outcome: A residual inflammatory and proteomic signature that persists in children treated from infancy, at the same restored CFTR function as later-treated patients, would show the inflammatory arm running partly independently of current CFTR activity.
refuting_outcome: Normalization of the airway proteome, cytokines and microbiome in the infant-initiated cohort would attribute the residual disease of later-treated patients to prior structural and microbial injury rather than to a CFTR-independent inflammatory program.

selected_evidence.snippet: Despite these improvements, proteomic and cytokine profiles remained distinct from healthy controls.

Loss of CFTR-mediated anion secretion (and secondary hyperabsorption of sodium and water) produces dehydrated, acidic, viscous airway surface liquid and pancreatic/biliary secretions. The resulting impaired mucociliary clearance, chronic bacterial airway infection, and obstructive secretions drive the progressive bronchiectatic lung disease, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, hepatobiliary disease, elevated sweat chloride, and male infertility (CBAVD) characteristic of cystic fibrosis. CFTR modulator therapies (correctors/potentiators, exemplified by elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor) that restore residual CFTR activity provide direct interventional validation of this canonical pathway.
assertion.notes: Retained as CANONICAL following independent assessment of the 2026 OpenScientist hypothesis-search report (see kb/hypotheses/Cystic_Fibrosis/canonical_cftr_loss_of_function_model/assessments/openscientist-assessment-by-codex.md; reconciliation tracked in issue #7325). The core mechanism is well supported by convergent evidence: newborn CF-pig airway-surface-liquid acidification impairs bacterial killing before infection or inflammation, and randomized/registry CFTR-modulator trials (ETI: ppFEV1 +9.9 across 11,151 registry patients) provide direct human interventional validation. Several report-level claims required narrowing rather than verbatim promotion: (1) as of the 2013 CFTR2 analysis, few of the nearly 2,000 then-reported CFTR variants had empirical evidence of disease causation, so an unqualified ">2,000 disease-causing variants" count conflates reported with clinically classified variants; CFTR2 has interpreted substantially more variants since, so any exact count must be dated to its source snapshot rather than asserted in the present tense; (2) bicarbonate secretion has been shown to be rate-limiting for host defense in mixed porcine airway epithelia and cell-culture systems, but this does not establish bicarbonate as the universal rate-limiting determinant over chloride across all human tissues and genotypes; (3) human monocyte-derived macrophages show direct CFTR-dependent defects, but a cited CFTR-depleted zebrafish neutrophil-recruitment finding traced the effect to epithelial oxidative signaling rather than immune-cell-autonomous CFTR dysfunction, so the two should not be conflated as one parallel immune mechanism; (4) residual airway inflammation and molecular abnormalities persisting after highly effective modulator therapy reflect incomplete correction of CFTR function rather than proof that inflammation becomes independent of ongoing CFTR dysfunction; and (5) next-generation vanzacaftor evidence of differential response in two previously unresponsive genotypes is from intestinal organoids, not yet a demonstrated clinical rescue.

assertion.description: Heterozygous de novo truncating SMC1A variants, X-linked. SMC1A encodes a core structural subunit of the cohesin complex, so this is a cohesinopathy and the gene is wired to the non-channelopathy lesion node. The allelic split matters clinically: missense and small in-frame SMC1A changes cause about 5 per cent of Cornelia de Lange syndrome, which dismech curates separately, whereas protein-truncating changes cause this epilepsy phenotype. assertion.name: DEE114
assertion.description: De novo missense SLC32A1 variants. SLC32A1 encodes the vesicular GABA transporter, which loads GABA into synaptic vesicles, so the lesion is presynaptic and inhibitory. Inherited missense variants in the same gene had already been linked to genetic epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, and this report establishes that de novo missense variants instead cause a DEE. Two mechanisms were demonstrated in a murine neuronal culture model: three variants lining the putative GABA transport pathway reduced quantal size, consistent with impaired vesicle filling, while an N-terminal variant left quantal size intact but raised presynaptic release probability.

selected_evidence.snippet: The main phenotype comprises moderate-to-severe intellectual disability, infantile-onset epilepsy within the first 18 months of life, and a choreiform, dystonic, or dyskinetic movement disorder.

assertion.name: F9
assertion.notes: F9 coding, splice, copy-number, and proximal promoter variants can cause disease. Activity rather than antigen concentration defines severity: some dysfunctional proteins retain cross-reacting antigen. Null alleles confer greater inhibitor risk than missense alleles. A single heterozygous pathogenic variant can cause disease in females; low factor levels can reflect skewed X inactivation, but blood-cell X-inactivation measurements do not directly establish hepatocyte mosaicism. assertion.hypothesis_label: Canonical F9 Deficiency / Intrinsic Coagulation Failure Model
assertion.description: Pathogenic F9 variants reduce FIX production or activity. FIX activated by FXIa or the tissue-factor/FVIIa complex normally combines with FVIIIa on activated platelet surfaces to activate factor X and support propagation of thrombin generation. Functional FIX deficiency impairs this amplification and fibrin hemostasis to a degree related to residual activity. Replacement, gene addition, and experimental gene correction support the causal role of F9; pharmacologic inhibition of anticoagulant pathways can bypass the defect.
assertion.notes: The full OpenScientist report was reviewed against its cited sources, additional primary literature, and GeneReviews. Retain CANONICAL, but replace universal abolition of thrombin with severity-dependent impairment. Both HOPE-B and BENEGENE-2 use FIX-Padua; their lead-in comparisons and distinct follow-up cohorts must not be pooled. A separate ten-person wild-type F9 AAV cohort has median 13-year follow-up. The report overlooked direct experimental evidence for collagen-IV-bound extravascular FIX and existing definitive ClinGen curation. Leyden regulation and inhibitor risk are valid refinements. Modifier associations do not explain a measured 10–15% of HB variance; mixed HA/HB platelet and bone observations do not establish a primary platelet lesion or direct FIX-to-osteoblast pathway. Mouse synovitis and bone results remain species-qualified. See the accompanying openscientist-assessment-by-codex.yaml for claim-level adjudication and unperformed analyses.

assertion.features: CBS-deficient homocystinuria is caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the CBS gene. assertion.name: CDK19

Neither a universal loss-of-function mechanism nor simple haploinsufficiency explains all reported variants.
